final_answer:
A HASH TABLE HANDLES COLLISIONS WHEN TWO KEYS PRODUCE THE SAME HASH VALUE. COMMON TECHNIQUES INCLUDE CHAINING AND OPEN ADDRESSING.

CHAINING STORES MULTIPLE ENTRIES IN THE SAME BUCKET USING A LINKED LIST (OR DYNAMIC ARRAY/OTHER STRUCTURE). WHEN A COLLISION OCCURS, THE ENTRY IS ADDED TO THE CHAIN. ADVANTAGES INCLUDE SIMPLER IMPLEMENTATION, LOWER DEGRADATION UNDER HIGH LOAD, AND EASY RESIZING. DISADVANTAGES INCLUDE INCREASED MEMORY USAGE DUE TO POINTERS AND POTENTIAL CACHE INEFFICIENCY FROM NON-CONTIGUOUS DATA.

OPEN ADDRESSING STORES ALL ENTRIES IN THE TABLE ITSELF. WHEN A COLLISION OCCURS, IT PROBES FOR AN EMPTY SLOT USING A SEQUENCE (LINEAR, QUADRATIC, DOUBLE HASHING). ADVANTAGES INCLUDE BETTER CACHE LOCALITY AND LOWER MEMORY OVERHEAD. DISADVANTAGES INCLUDE HIGHER COMPLEXITY, POTENTIAL PERFORMANCE DEGRADATION AT HIGH LOAD, AND THE NEED FOR CAREFUL RESIZING STRATEGIES.

TRADE-OFFS: CHAINING TENDS TO PERFORM BETTER FOR MANY COLLISIONS BUT USES MORE MEMORY; OPEN ADDRESSING IS MORE MEMORY-EFFICIENT BUT CAN SUFFER FROM WORSE WORST-CASE PERFORMANCE IF NOT IMPLEMENTED CAUTIOUSLY.
